prompt: 句中的 crucial 最接近哪個意思？
text: Checking the date on the ticket is crucial; a wrong date means you cannot board.
options: 非常重要、不可忽略的
有點無聊的
價格便宜的
很容易忘記的

wrong.有點無聊的: 句子說日期錯了就不能登機，可見這件事重要，不是無聊。
wrong.價格便宜的: crucial 談的是重要程度，和價格無關。
wrong.很容易忘記的: 句子沒有說容易忘記，只強調檢查日期的必要性。

why: 後半句說日期錯就不能登機，表示這個檢查關係成敗，所以 crucial 是「關鍵的、非常重要的」。
tip: 後面接嚴重後果，前面的形容詞常是「關鍵」。
say: Checking the date on the ticket is crucial.

prompt: 選出最適合填入空格的字。
text: Before you choose an answer, _____ the chart with the paragraph to see whether they agree.
options: cross-reference
cross-country
cross-legged
cross-out the

wrong.cross-country: cross-country 是「越野的」，不能當動詞拿來對照圖表與文章。
wrong.cross-legged: cross-legged 是「盤腿的」形容詞，句子需要動詞。
wrong.cross-out the: cross out 是「劃掉」，而且 the 重複，句意也不是對照兩份資料。

why: cross-reference 當動詞是「交叉對照」，正好符合把圖表和段落互相比對的動作。
tip: 圖文題要把兩份資料來回對照，用 cross-reference。
say: Cross-reference the chart with the paragraph.

prompt: 哪一句的 evaluation 用法正確？
options: The teacher gave an evaluation of my essay.
The teacher evaluation my essay yesterday.
The teacher gave a evaluate of my essay.
The teacher is evaluation my essay now.
answer: The teacher gave an evaluation of my essay.

wrong.The teacher evaluation my essay yesterda: evaluation 是名詞，不能直接當過去式動詞；動詞要用 evaluated。
evaluate 是動詞，名詞要用 evaluation，而且 e 開頭要用 an。
is 後面接名詞 evaluation 變成「老師是評估」，語意不通；進行式要用 evaluating。

why: gave an evaluation of 是「給了……的評估」，名詞 evaluation 前面用 an，後面用 of 接對象。
tip: evaluate 是動詞，evaluation 是名詞，別混用。
say: The teacher gave an evaluation of my essay.

prompt: 閱讀測驗題目問：「作者的哪一句話是在『指出』數據來源？」哪個動詞最適合代換 point out？
options: indicate
ignore
delay
borrow

wrong.ignore: ignore 是「忽視」，意思剛好相反。
wrong.delay: delay 是「延遲」，和指出資訊無關。
wrong.borrow: borrow 是「借入」，不能用來表示指出事實。

why: indicate 有「指出、顯示」的意思，常用在 The data indicate that... 這類句型。
tip: indicate = point out，後面常接 that 子句。
say: The data indicate that sales went up.

prompt: 哪一句把 assume 用得最自然？
options: I assume that the test starts at nine.
I assume the test to starts at nine.
I assume of the test starts at nine.
I am assume the test starts at nine.
answer: I assume that the test starts at nine.

to 後面要接原形動詞，不能寫 to starts。
assume 是及物動詞，後面不加 of。
am 與 assume 不能同時當動詞，應直接說 I assume。

why: assume 後面可直接接 that 子句，表示「我假設、我認為」某件事成立。
tip: assume 後面直接接 that 子句，不加 of。
say: I assume that the test starts at nine.

prompt: 這句話的 explicit 是什麼意思？
text: The rules were explicit: no phones may be used during the test.
options: 規定寫得清楚明確
規定很難讀懂
規定已被取消
規定只適用老師

wrong.規定很難讀懂: explicit 是「清楚明說的」，不是難懂。
wrong.規定已被取消: 句子仍然在說不可使用手機，並沒有取消。
wrong.規定只適用老師: 句子針對 test 期間的人，沒有限定老師。

why: 冒號後面直接寫出具體禁止事項，表示規定毫不含糊，這就是 explicit。
tip: explicit 是直接講明；相反字是 implicit。

prompt: 同學說：「我覺得這個推論不成立，因為證據不夠。」哪句英文最符合？
options: I don't think that conclusion is valid; the evidence is too thin.
I don't think that conclusion is valuable; the evidence is too thick.
I think that conclusion is value; the evidence is thin.
I don't valid that conclusion because evidence.
answer: I don't think that conclusion is valid; the evidence is too thin.

wrong.I don't think that conclusion is valuabl: valuable 是「有價值的」，不是「有效、成立的」；thick 也和證據不足相反。
wrong.I think that conclusion is value; the ev: value 是名詞或動詞，不能放在 is 後面當形容詞，而且語意變成肯定。
wrong.I don't valid that conclusion because ev: valid 是形容詞，不能當動詞；because 後也缺完整子句。

why: valid 的意思是「合理、站得住腳的」，與 the evidence is too thin 搭配，正好表示推論不成立。
tip: valid 形容論點有效；valuable 是有價值。
say: I don't think that conclusion is valid.

text: Please give me a _____ answer: is the museum open on Monday, yes or no?
options: precise
vague
random
fragile

wrong.vague: vague 是「模糊的」，而題目要求 yes or no 的明確答案。
wrong.random: random 是「隨機的」，不符合要求精確回答的語意。
wrong.fragile: fragile 是「易碎的」，不能修飾 answer。

why: 對方要求只回答是或否，需要的是 precise「精準、不含糊」的答案。
tip: 要明確答案就說 a precise answer。
say: Please give me a precise answer.

prompt: 這段文字中，文章用 benchmark 最可能想表示什麼？
text: The school's reading score became the benchmark for all other classes.
options: 其他班級用來比較的標準
其他班級必須放棄的目標
一張沒人要坐的長椅
一次突然取消的考試
answer: 其他班級用來比較的標準

wrong.其他班級必須放棄的目標: benchmark 是比較用的標準，不是要放棄的目標。
wrong.一張沒人要坐的長椅: bench 雖是長椅，但 benchmark 整體是「基準」，句中談的是分數。
wrong.一次突然取消的考試: 句子沒有提到取消考試，benchmark 也不是考試。

why: for all other classes 表示其他班用它來對照，所以 benchmark 是「基準、標竿」。
tip: benchmark 不是長椅，而是比較時的標竿。
say: The score became the benchmark for all classes.

prompt: 閱讀時你要說明「根據上下文，這個字應該是正面意思」，哪句英文最自然？
options: Judging from the context, the word must be positive.
Judging from the contest, the word must be positive.
Judge from the context, the word must positive.
Judging for context, word must be positive is.
answer: Judging from the context, the word must be positive.

wrong.Judging from the contest, the word must: contest 是「比賽」，context 才是「上下文」，兩字拼法相近容易誤用。
wrong.Judge from the context, the word must po: Judge 開頭語法不通順，且 must 後面缺 be。
wrong.Judging for context, word must be positi: for 要改成 from，且句尾多了 is，語序不正確。

why: Judging from the context 是常見片語，意為「從上下文判斷」，後面接完整子句。
tip: Judging from the context 是閱讀推測詞義的好片語。
say: Judging from the context, the word must be positive.

prompt: 哪一句的 support 用法正確？
options: The graph supports the writer's claim.
The graph support the writer's claim.
The graph supporting the writer's claim is.
The graph is support to writer's claim.
answer: The graph supports the writer's claim.

主詞 graph 是單數，現在式動詞要加 s，應為 supports。
wrong.The graph supporting the writer's claim: supporting 加上 is 放句尾，語序混亂，沒有形成完整句子。
is 後面不能直接接動詞原形 support，而且 writer's 前缺 the。

why: graph 是第三人稱單數，現在簡單式的動詞 support 要變成 supports。
tip: 單數主詞加現在式動詞，記得補 s。
say: The graph supports the writer's claim.

prompt: 考試時你想說：「這題的陷阱可能致命，請多小心。」哪一句最合適？
options: That trap can be fatal to your score, so be careful.
That trap can be fatty to your score, so be careful.
That trap can fate your score, so be careful.
That trap can be fatal for your score careful.
answer: That trap can be fatal to your score, so be careful.

wrong.That trap can be fatty to your score, so: fatty 是「油膩的」，fatal 才是「致命的」。
wrong.That trap can fate your score, so be car: fate 是名詞「命運」，這裡不能當動詞用。
wrong.That trap can be fatal for your score ca: 結尾缺 so be，careful 單獨放在句尾文法不完整。

why: fatal 表示後果嚴重，be fatal to 常用來形容對成績或計畫造成重大傷害。
tip: fatal 是致命的；fatty 是油膩的，別拼錯。
say: That trap can be fatal to your score.
